title: RWB-E2-031 version 2 app slice: the drift step and its Schedule, the segment source, the decision-log read, the notice, the policy values, the migration scope, the element change, the screen states, the login, the route path, the range limits and the two windows are not named by the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 031 Agent monitoring dashboard v2 E3d v1.md (legacy story RWB-E2-031); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P10 Agent runtime v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P10 Agent runtime v3.md (A2.6); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 16, 41, 43 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: The legacy story is written against objects of the monolith that have no target name in the sources. It names the JOB-15 step agentDrift, the data lake table agent_run_daily, recovery_case.product_group and recovery_case.region_code, the in-process P7 DecisionLogQuery.byAgentVersion, the P6 notification interface, the Platform administration R right, a migration V10_007__agent_run_segment.sql that adds segment columns and a data lake copy that is removed. Architecture v5 gives the service, its schema, its topic, its queue and its REST base but no Schedule step names beyond the baseline, no gateway-bff route path, no service login name and no decision-log filter or override-reason element. The target place of the drift step, the source of the segment, the shape of the decision-log read, the notice operation, the policy values of the drift rule, the scope of the migration, the kind of the element change, the screen states, the login, the route path, the two range limits and the two acceptance windows are therefore defaulted, and each default is recorded as an assumption row.
evidence: Legacy sections 4 and 12 name the JOB-15 steps and the lake table; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting with no agent step; slide 37 removes the data lake; slides 41 and 16 give schema rwb_agent, base /api/recovery/agent/v1, topic rwb.agent.events.v1 and queue rwb-agent but no Schedule, route, login or filter names; TSD P10 T-A.1 API-P10-009 gives the query and the right as Rules and parameters R while the legacy story names Platform administration R
area: P10 rwb-agent - agent monitoring dashboard version 2, app slice
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect
proposed: Accept the defaults: the drift step joins the baseline Schedule as the agentDrift activity, the segment is read from the run row, the override and decision-quality figures come from the decision-log read of rwb-decision, the notice leaves through rwb-comms, the drift values stay approved policy rows, the migration adds indexes only, the element change is additive within major version 1, the screen states are read from the policy mode, the login and the route path are fixed with the deployment and edge stories, the two range limits are configuration values and the two windows are 7 calendar days each.

title: RWB-E2-031 version 2 contract slice: the decision-log filter and override element, the notice operation, the name of the read right, the paging and member types, the route path, the login and the Schedule step names are not fixed by the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 031 Agent monitoring dashboard v2 E3d v1.md (legacy story RWB-E2-031); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P7 rwb-decision (Decision and rules)/RWB P7 E2005 CON Decision log query API for audit - contract v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P10 Agent runtime v2.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 16, 41 and 44
section: Contract sections 3, 7 (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7), 11, 12.1-12.6, 15
description: The published decision-log contract of rwb-decision declares the query of AC3 of its legacy story and its answer page, but the agent-version filter and the override-reason element the monitoring key needs are additive to it and carry no name in the sources. The notification operation of rwb-comms has no path in any source. The right of the read is named Rules and parameters R by the TSD and Platform administration R by the legacy story, and no source states which name is authoritative. The page size, the cursor form and the exact types of the rate and amount members beyond four decimals are not fixed. The gateway-bff route path in front of the read and the name of the service login are not given. The Schedule keeps its baseline name and its steps carry the baseline names plus the legacy step name. The contract fixes each of these with one default and one assumption row.
evidence: RWB-P7-E2005-CON section 12.1 declares GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} with query parameters of its own AC3 and no agent-version filter; TSD P10 T-A.1 API-P10-009 gives query agent, segment, version, from and to and the right Rules and parameters R; the legacy story gives Platform administration R; Arch v5 slide 16 names the rwb-agent topic and queue but no operation of rwb-comms; no source names the route path or the login
area: P10 rwb-agent - agent monitoring dashboard version 2, contract slice
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-comms and rwb-access
proposed: Accept the defaults: the decision-log read is consumed with the agent-version filter and the override reason as an additive change to RWB-P7-E2005-CON, the notice is named at the boundary without a path, the right is called the right of the read with both names recorded, the paging is one page size and a cursor with four-decimal rate and amount members, the route path and the login are fixed with the edge and deployment stories, and the Schedule keeps the baseline name with the four steps of the contract.

title: RWB-E2-031 version 2 deployment slice: the route path, the login secret, the topology and budget, the notice operation, the Schedule registration detail and the model gateway egress are not fixed by the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 031 Agent monitoring dashboard v2 E3d v1.md (legacy story RWB-E2-031); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P10 Agent runtime v2.md (T5.1 INT-23, T7); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 16, 20, 41 and 44; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.7
description: The deployment slice has to name values no source fixes: the gateway-bff route path in front of the three reads, the name of the per-service login secret, the deployment topology with host, SKU, budget, replica counts, resource sizes and probe timings, the notification operation of rwb-comms, the detail of the Schedule registration hook, and the host and policy of the single egress to the model gateway. The sources give the naming rule, the queue, the namespace, the topic and the private endpoint in principle, and they give no path, no secret name, no topology and no budget. Each is defaulted and recorded.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives the naming rule for schema, base, topic and queue only; slide 20 gives gateway-bff as the only entry for staff screens with no path; TSD P10 T5.1 gives INT-23 as a private endpoint in the SCB tenant with no host; TSD P10 T-B lists DL35 deployment slots as open; no source names a login secret or a topology
area: P10 rwb-agent - agent monitoring dashboard version 2, deployment slice
owner_role: DevOps engineer with the platform administrator and the security administrator
proposed: Accept the defaults: the route path is fixed with the edge story, the login is referenced through a secret reference whose name is fixed with the platform administrator, the topology and budget are values files reviewed at release, the notice is reached through its contract, the Schedule is created or updated idempotently by the release, and the single egress is the private endpoint of the model gateway declared once for the run path.
